summary: Martian Explorers is an interactive, child-friendly storytelling platform developed by Team Chanda Taray for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, addressing the challenge “Abandoned but Not Forgotten.” Designed for children aged 5–12, the platform transforms the stories of retired Mars exploration equipment into engaging animated experiences. Through robotic explorers such as Opportunity, Ingenuity, and Phoenix, children discover their missions, achievements, and contributions to space exploration. By combining authentic NASA information, simplified storytelling, interactive scenes, and child-friendly visuals, the project makes space science more accessible and enjoyable for young learners. Martian Explorers aims to preserve the stories of overlooked exploration technology, spark curiosity about Mars and robotics, and encourage early scientific literacy. Its ultimate vision is to inspire the next generation of space explorers by showing that every machine has a mission and every mission deserves a story.
details:
Martian Explorers, developed by Team Chanda Taray, is an interactive, web-based educational storytelling platform created for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 under the challenge “Abandoned but Not Forgotten.” Our project addresses the gap between traditional, information-heavy space archives and the way young children engage with science. Designed for children aged 5–12, it transforms the stories of retired Mars exploration equipment into animated, interactive, and educational experiences.

How It Works

The platform takes children on a storybook journey through the history of Mars exploration. Users enter the storybook, meet a robotic explorer, explore different animated scenes, interact with visual elements, and discover real scientific facts behind its mission. The initial stories feature three significant explorers:

  • Opportunity: A Mars rover that investigated rocks and soil for evidence of past water and operated far beyond its planned 90 sols.
  • Ingenuity: The helicopter that achieved the first powered, controlled flight on another planet, completing 72 flights.
  • Phoenix: A lander that studied Martian soil, ice, and atmosphere in the planet's arctic plains.

We transform verified NASA mission information into simplified story moments, combining scientific knowledge with creative narratives and child-friendly visuals.

Audience Research and Creative Approach

Our creative decisions were informed by research into our target audience's interests, preferences, and psychology. Since the platform is designed for children aged 5–12, we considered how young learners engage with characters, visuals, storytelling, and interactive experiences.

We adopted a Pixar-inspired animation style to create expressive, approachable characters and visually engaging environments that make scientific subjects feel more relatable. We also incorporated the breaking the fourth wall technique, allowing characters to communicate directly with the audience and create a more engaging storytelling experience. This helps transform children from passive viewers into active participants in the stories.

Our aim was to combine entertainment with education, making scientific information easier to connect with, understand, and remember.

Tools, Technologies and Software

Our team used a combination of AI-assisted tools, creative software, and modern web development technologies:

AI Tools: Gemini, ChatGPT, Canva AI and Google AI Studio.

Design and Creative Software: Canva was used for visual design and presentation development.

Programming Languages and Frameworks:

  • React – Front-end development and user interface.
  • TypeScript – Application logic and structured development.
  • HTML – Web page structure.
  • CSS – Styling and visual presentation.

Deployment and Hosting: Vercel and Netlify were used as web deployment and hosting platforms. The project website is published on Vercel.

Benefits and Intended Impact

Martian Explorers makes planetary science more accessible to children by replacing purely technical explanations with relatable characters and interactive storytelling. It encourages curiosity about robotics, astronomy, and space exploration while building early scientific literacy. More importantly, it gives recognition to overlooked machines whose missions contributed valuable knowledge to humanity.

Design Considerations

Throughout development, we considered the target audience's age, interests, attention span, comprehension level, visual engagement, scientific accuracy, and ease of interaction. We aimed to balance authentic NASA information with imaginative storytelling without compromising educational value.

Future Possibilities

We envision expanding the platform with character voices, multilingual narration, more stories about lunar and deep-space missions, interactive quizzes, mission timelines, and classroom activities.

Our vision is simple: Every machine has a mission, and every mission deserves a story.
